allowListChallenge.credentialShapedOrOperatorPrivate: None credential-shaped. Operator-private-ish entries are all paths a same-uid process could derive anyway and are needed: XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (/run/user/1000, where secretsd's socket lives — `secrets` in omp_launch_prefix needs it; it is also where SSH_AUTH_SOCK/gpg sockets would live, but the pane is not told those names), SECRETSD_SOCK (unset on this box), TMUX_TMPDIR (lets a pane address the production server's socket — same-uid access the spec's Rejected section already accepts), HOME/USER/LOGNAME/SHELL/TERM/TZ/LANG/LC_*, MISE_*, OMP_PROFILE/PI_PROFILE, proxy/CA policy, PATH (replaced by mise's).
allowListChallenge.missingForAPane: Nothing observed missing: controller, architect, sub-architect, planner and implementer all completed turns; `secrets ... -- omp` resolved the provider keys inside the pane (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY present only in the omp child); `legion` CLI (status/state/handoff complete), Dispatch tools (DISPATCH_URL/DISPATCH_TOKEN_FILE), jj (status/new/split/bookmark), `jj git push` through the credential helper, all worked. Pagers are not needed (gh/jj/git see no tty). JJ_CONFIG is intentionally absent: with it unset jj's default user chain is ~/.jjconfig.toml (-> ~/.dotfiles/.jjconfig.toml) : ~/.config/jj/config.toml, so the operator's shared jj config is still loaded and the extension's attribution overlay chains on top (jj-attribution.ts userConfigChain) — no regression, and the operator session's own attribution overlay no longer leaks into daemon-made commits.
allowListChallenge.isSecretLikeNameVsMise: On this box `env -i HOME PATH USER MISE_DATA_DIR OMP_PROFILE=legion mise env --json` emits exactly AGENT_EVAL_VERSION CARGO_HOME GOBIN GOROOT PATH RUSTUP_HOME RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN (mise.toml [env] sets only AGENT_EVAL_VERSION); none matches /(?:_SECRET|_TOKEN|_GRANT|_API_KEY|_PASSWORD)(?:_FILE)?$|PRIVATE_KEY/. The regex anchors the suffix (TOKENIZER passes, environment.test.ts pins it). A future mise [env] GITHUB_TOKEN (the usual rate-limit trick) or CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN would be dropped — correctly, those are credentials a pane must not inherit; a pane's `gh` gets its own per-call token from the shim.

adversarial.severity: high (deployment, outside this PR's code; blocks the spec's 'No model-driven process can read a daemon-only secret' requirement and makes acceptance 5's rotation ineffective as-is)
adversarial.finding: The two App private keys are AGENT-tier secrets in secretsd, so any pane can fetch them without a YubiKey touch through the same `secrets` client the omp_launch_prefix relies on — the allow-list closes the environment door, but this door is wide open and independent of the pane environment.
adversarial.reproduction: From this production tester pane (LEGION_ROLE=tester), value never printed: $ secrets GH_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64 GH_REVIEW_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64 -- sh -c 'printf "agent key bytes=%s review key bytes=%s\n" "$(printf %s "$GH_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64" | wc -c)" "$(printf %s "$GH_REVIEW_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64" | wc -c)"' -> agent key bytes=2237 review key bytes=2237. Same under a fully scrubbed environment: $ env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=$PATH USER=$USER XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR secrets GH_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64 -- sh -c '...' -> agent key bytes=2237. `secrets list` shows both keys without a '(human tier ...)' marker while e.g. GITHUB_ADMIN_PAT is human-tier.
adversarial.consequence: The production daemon's 06:06 mitigation (private_key_command = `secrets GH_*_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64 -- ...`, keys no longer in the daemon's environ: verified /proc/2833124/environ PRIVATE_KEY count 0) depends on exactly this agent-tier readability, so the rotated keys of acceptance 5 will be readable by every pane the moment they are stored the same way. Not fixed here (not this PR's surface). Options for the architect/Sami: give the daemon its own secretsd identity/scope (secretsd already has per-session tokens: the daemon could hold a session whose grants panes do not share), or read the keys from a file owned by a separate uid/service account, or run the daemon as a different user than the panes.

adversarial.finding: tmux.conf `set-environment -g` reaches a freshly-forked server's very FIRST pane and every later pane until the next daemon boot: tmux sources ~/.tmux.conf before it spawns the first window, TPM runs `tmux set-environment -g TMUX_PLUGIN_MANAGER_PATH ~/.tmux/plugins/`, and the boot-time scrub has already run (there was no server to scrub). Confirmed on a scratch server (first pane pid 3485511 TMUX_PLUGIN_MANAGER_PATH=1, second pane 1) and on the phase-B rig (controller %1 and root architect %2 both TMUX_PLUGIN_MANAGER_PATH=1; show-environment -g lists it; the server's own /proc environ does not). It is scrubbed on the next boot (phase A named it). Matters only if an operator's tmux.conf ever `set-environment -g`s or `run-shell`-exports a credential; on this box it is a plugin path. Closing it would mean starting the private server with `-f /dev/null` (skip the operator's tmux.conf entirely) or re-running the scrub once right after the first new-session forks the server. Report only.
adversarial.reproduction: $ env -i HOME PATH USER TMUX_TMPDIR TERM=tmux-256color tmux -L legion-l74tscratch new-session -d -s legion-l74tscratch -n first 'sleep 120'; p1=$(tmux -L legion-l74tscratch display-message -p -t legion-l74tscratch:first '#{pane_pid}'); tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/$p1/environ | grep -c TMUX_PLUGIN_MANAGER_PATH -> 1

adversarial.finding: Per-pane -e pairs: inspected every non-allow-listed name in a live pane's environ (LEGION_*, DISPATCH_*, ENVOY_*, GH_*, GIT_*): values are URLs, <state_dir> paths (LEGION_BOOT_TOKEN_FILE, LEGION_GRANT_FILE, DISPATCH_TOKEN_FILE, GH_CONFIG_DIR), empties (GH_TOKEN= GITHUB_TOKEN= GH_HOST=) or small literals — no secret rides tmux's argv. worker-shim spawns OMP with Bun.spawn and no env option (inherits the pane env, adds nothing). The `secrets ... -- omp` launch prefix places the provider keys in the omp child only (pane shell and shim: 0), by design.

The scrub is boot-time only: an operator `tmux -L legion-<project> set-environment -g NAME v` (or -t) after boot reaches every later pane until the next restart; `update-environment ''` only stops attaches from doing it implicitly. Same-uid /proc reads remain: a pane can read /proc/<daemon pid>/environ (on the rig the daemon's environ carried both keys; in production it no longer does) and <state_dir>/secrets/* — both accepted by the spec's Rejected section.

Unaffected by the allow-list (the daemon's jj resolves the same user config with or without JJ_CONFIG).
